title: Optimizer Orchestrator: offline suggestion engine and validated rollback for private deployments
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Private/VPC/on-prem customers cannot safely accept automated batching/caching recommendations that assume internet-accessible telemetry, service accounts, or relaxed permissions. We need an orchestrator that can generate cost-saving suggestions, validate their safety under restrictive environments, and apply changes via a vetted, reversible path.

Scope: build an "optimizer orchestrator" service and a CLI flow for private deployments that: 1) produces batching and KV-caching recommendations derived from local traces and lightweight sampling; 2) runs an offline validation simulation that models latency and KV-cache hit-rate impact without changing runtime state; 3) generates a signed, auditable plan that can be applied with a guarded executor supporting atomic apply + commit + rollback; 4) enforces org policy rules (RBAC, quantization/latency constraints, KMS-only key usage) before permitting apply.

Why different from existing tools: avoid assumptions that agents or telemetry can POST to hosted endpoints. The orchestrator must work in fully air-gapped environments using only on-node traces, periodic secure uploads to a customer-managed telemetry bucket, and local policy engines. The user experience should prioritize conservative suggestions with explainable regressions and a deterministic dry-run model so SREs can sign off before any commit.
acceptance_criteria: Generate batching and KV-cache suggestions from local trace samples and store as a signed plan (JSON + metadata)
Offline validation simulator that models latency and token-cost delta; output must include worst-case and median projections
Policy engine hooks that reject plans violating RBAC or KMS constraints, with clear error codes
Apply CLI that supports --preview, --apply, --commit, --rollback and produces an immutable audit record in the customer audit log
Rollback path verified by integration test that simulates a failed commit and restores prior config within SLO (5 minutes)
work_log: 2026-02-10 - Ticket created; initial scoping with PM (Ravi Patel) and Design (Eden Cho).

2026-02-15 - Spike completed: proof-of-concept sampler that extracts trace sketches from local runtime (repo: runtime/trace-sampler). Found that 90% of short-requests (<128 tokens) show predictable batching gains.
2026-02-20 - Meeting with Security: confirmed KMS-only key policy for on-prem customers and requirement for signed plans. Security requested HSM-compatible signing (linked requirement).
2026-02-24 - Implemented first offline simulator prototype (branch: optimizer-orch/sim-v1). Simulator takes plan and trace-sample and outputs token-cost projection and latency hazard cases.

2026-03-01 - UX review: added --preview output format that includes a human-readable explainability section for SRE signoff. Design suggested 'confidence buckets' to avoid numeric-only recommendations.

2026-03-05 - Internal engineering review: adjusted apply flow to write a pre-commit snapshot to a local immutable file store and emit an audit event to local audit log. Action: add integration tests for rollback determinism.
decisions: Use conservative defaults: suggestions will default to 'optimize-aggressiveness: low' for VPC/private profiles to minimize regressions.
Offline simulator will model both median and 95th-percentile latency to surface tail risks for latency-sensitive routes.
Signed plan format will be JSON with base64-signed manifest; signature scheme will support both software keys and HSM-backed keys (customer choice).
No external telemetry required for core validation. Optionally support secure, customer-managed S3/GCS uploads for richer analysis if the customer enables it.
notes: Follow-ups: add bounded experiment runner to run canary applies in isolated on-prem rings (next ticket).
Design must add an 'explainability' view in Console private mode showing sample traces and why a suggestion improves cost per-token.
Ops: schedule a dry-run with customer 'Acme Health' in their staging VPC to validate HSM-key signing and audit artifacts.
Testing: create failure-mode scenarios where KV cache purge coincides with rollout to ensure rollback restores prior cache configuration without data loss.
